A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PCFM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison across additions, relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original PDE-generation experiments, numerical comparisons in Table 3, and collocation, total-variation and penalty-weight ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds PDM comparisons, runtime measurements, an intermediate-projection ablation and out-of-distribution Burgers results.

M1.justification: Equations A.1 and 34 revise the iterative projection from a correction around the current iterate to an update anchored at the original prediction u1, including an additional Jacobian-displacement term. This changes the specified solver procedure locally; the pretrained model, forward shooting, OT interpolation and relaxed correction framework remain.

E1.justification: The four PDE families and original IC/BC tasks remain. Appendix L.4 adds a Burgers distribution-shift scenario, describing training centers in [0.4, 0.6] and test centers in [0, 0.2] and [0.8, 1]. This extends input-condition coverage within an existing task.

E2.justification: PDM is newly evaluated across all five main Table 3 settings, adding a nonlinear projection-based comparator alongside the retained ECI, DiffusionPDE, D-Flow and FFM methods. Appendix H describes its implementation and flow-model adaptation. Table 6 additionally introduces a final-projection-only control, substantially strengthening the relevant comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix H changes the stated Navier–Stokes budget from 200 to 100 Euler steps; unchanged scores do not establish whether experiments were rerun. New evaluation designs include runtime/memory measurements at 100 steps and zero penalty, controlled batch sizes on one V100 GPU, final-only projection controls, and 200-step OOD testing.

E4.justification: V2 adds an intermediate-versus-final-only projection ablation across four PDEs, a Burgers OOD robustness test, and runtime/memory and projection-overhead analyses. These test component necessity, generalization and practical cost. The earlier collocation, TVD and penalty-weight analyses are retained, with appendix renumbering.

E5.justification: Both versions report sample variability through mean-plus/minus-one-standard-deviation residual plots. V2's checklist points to existing plots and SMSE but introduces no repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or new uncertainty-estimation procedure. Adding PDM panels uses the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds PDM scores and runtime, projection-ablation and OOD results while retaining the original Table 3 values and TVD table values. PDM changes the Heat ranking: its FPD is 0.17 versus PCFM's 1.22, and its SMSE is 0.02 versus 0.937 in the table's 10^-2 units. These are new comparisons, not improvements in PCFM between versions.

T1.justification: The projection iteration used in Theorem A.1's proof and Appendix I's Equation 34 is mathematically revised to reference the original prediction. This is a substantive local correction, not equivalent notation. The theorem's assumptions and stated guarantee, Proposition 3.1 and the tangent-space proposition remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of zero-shot nonlinear equality-constraint enforcement without retraining, improved PDE generation and up to 99.5% error reduction. V2's introductory machine-precision wording makes explicit a qualification already present in v1's theorem; the added appendix evidence does not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly defines hard constraints in terms of solver and machine precision, explains PDM's poorer nonlinear results through over-constraining intermediate states, and interprets the new ablation as evidence that guidance reduces trajectory drift. It also adds interpretations of OOD generalization and computational overhead. Existing equality-only and scalability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies Python and experimental Julia repository links absent from v1, describes the PDM implementation/adaptation, and adds concrete inference hardware, batch sizes, memory measurements and projection timings. These materially expand access and practical reproducibility information beyond the retained dataset and training recipes. The PDFs establish the disclosures, not the contents of the linked repositories.

R1.justification: V2 adds Christopher et al.'s projected diffusion models and Utkarsh et al.'s end-to-end probabilistic hard-constraint framework. The related-work discussion newly distinguishes PCFM's terminal-directed guidance from PDM's projections of intermediate samples. The broader positioning and relationship to ECI remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section organization remain intact. V2 makes localized terminology and explanatory edits, subdivides Appendix E, inserts and renumbers Appendix L subsections, adds a NeurIPS checklist, and updates the publication footer. This is an expansion within the existing narrative rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: Table 3 and Figures 2, 3 and 5–8 gain PDM columns or panels, with revised color scales in several Burgers displays. Four new tables present runtime/memory, projection timing, the final-only ablation and OOD results. Existing figures are repositioned, while the original TVD table is retained as Table 7.

improvement.justification: The PDM comparison, final-only control, OOD test, runtime measurements and code links strengthen evidence and reproducibility beyond v1. However, Section 4.1 still claims superiority on every linear-task metric despite PDM's better Heat SMSE and FPD, Table 3 contains contradictory omission notes, and revised Equation 34 is not reconciled with Equation 33. These reporting and mathematical inconsistencies limit the net quality gain.
